title: Arduino Uno Board
summary: The brain of a beginner IoT project.
key_points: Uno uses the ATmega328P microcontroller and 5 V logic.
14 digital pins (6 can do PWM) and 6 analog inputs (A0–A5).
Programs (sketches) have setup() that runs once and loop() that repeats forever.

quiz.question: Which function runs only once when the Arduino starts?
What is the logic voltage of Arduino Uno?
How many analog input pins does Uno have?
Which function repeats again and again?

notes.principle: A microcontroller combines a processor, memory and input/output pins on one board. Arduino Uno runs a stored program and controls connected components.
notes.working: The ATmega328P executes the sketch uploaded through USB. Digital pins read HIGH/LOW signals, analog inputs measure changing voltages, and PWM pins can control output power.
applications: Reading sensors and controlling LEDs or motors
advantages: Beginner-friendly IDE and large learning community
USB programming and clear pin labels
safety: Check the board pinout and voltage before wiring.
Do not short 5 V to GND or power motors directly from I/O pins.

title: Ultrasonic Sensor (HC-SR04)
key_points: TRIG starts a measurement; ECHO returns a pulse whose width depends on distance.
Distance (cm) = duration × 0.034 ÷ 2.
Working range is roughly 2 cm to 400 cm.

quiz.question: Which HC-SR04 pin starts a measurement?
Why do we divide by 2 in the distance formula?
quiz.answer: Sound travels to the object and back
options: Sound travels to the object and back

quiz.question: What does HC-SR04 use to measure distance?

notes.principle: HC-SR04 measures distance from the time taken by an ultrasonic sound pulse to travel to an object and return as an echo.
notes.working: A short trigger pulse starts an ultrasonic burst. The Echo pin stays HIGH for the round-trip travel time; distance in centimetres is approximately echo time in microseconds divided by 58.
advantages: Simple digital trigger and echo interface
Useful over a practical short range
disadvantages: Soft or angled surfaces may reflect sound poorly
Readings can be affected by temperature and nearby objects
Not ideal for very small or distant targets
safety: Use the correct supply voltage and common ground.
Keep the sensor dry and avoid pointing it at people or animals at close range.

title: IR Sensor

english.query: IR sensor Arduino tutorial for beginners

key_points: An IR LED sends infrared light; a photodiode catches the reflection.
Most obstacle modules give LOW on OUT when an object is detected.
The small blue potentiometer on the module adjusts sensitivity.

quiz.question: Most IR obstacle modules output what when an object is detected?
A good use of an IR sensor is…
Which pin gives the detection signal?

notes.principle: An infrared sensor detects infrared light emitted or reflected by nearby objects.
notes.working: A typical reflective IR module has an IR LED and photodiode/phototransistor. Reflected IR changes the receiver signal; a comparator may convert it into a digital output.
disadvantages: Performance depends on surface colour and reflectivity
Sunlight and other IR sources can cause interference
safety: Avoid looking directly into high-power IR emitters.
Adjust sensitivity in the intended lighting conditions.

title: Temperature Sensor
key_points: LM35 gives 10 mV for every 1 °C.
analogRead() returns 0–1023 for 0–5 V.
Temperature = voltage × 100.

notes.principle: A temperature sensor converts temperature into an electrical quantity such as voltage, resistance or a digital value.
notes.working: The sensor element changes its electrical characteristics with temperature. The controller reads the analog or digital output and converts it using the sensor data sheet.
advantages: Can be combined with fans or alarms
safety: Observe the sensor operating range.
Do not expose low-voltage modules to hot surfaces or liquids unless rated for it.

title: Temperature & Humidity Sensor
key_points: DHT11 measures temperature and humidity with one data wire.
Read it about once every 2 seconds – it is a slow sensor.
Use isnan() to detect a failed reading.

quiz.question: How often should DHT11 be read?

notes.principle: A temperature-humidity sensor measures air temperature and relative humidity using sensing elements and provides calibrated digital data.
notes.working: A sensor such as DHT11/DHT22 samples its internal elements and sends a digital data frame to the microcontroller using a one-wire-style timing protocol.
advantages: Two environmental measurements in one module
disadvantages: Condensation and incorrect wiring affect readings
safety: Keep the sensor within its humidity and temperature ratings.
Do not immerse a non-waterproof module.

title: LDR / Light Sensor
key_points: LDR = Light Dependent Resistor: resistance drops in bright light.
A module (or voltage divider) turns this into a voltage Arduino can read.
Use a threshold value to decide “dark” or “bright”.

quiz.question: In bright light the LDR resistance…
Why connect an LDR to an analog pin?

notes.principle: An LDR changes resistance according to the amount of light falling on it; brighter light usually means lower resistance.
notes.working: The LDR is connected with a fixed resistor as a voltage divider. The controller reads the divider voltage using an analog input and compares it with a threshold.
disadvantages: Readings depend on divider resistor and light spectrum
safety: Use a suitable resistor to limit current.
Do not connect an LDR directly across a supply without considering current.

title: Soil Moisture Sensor
summary: Estimate how wet the soil is.
key_points: The probe’s electrical behaviour changes with water in the soil.
On common modules a wetter soil gives a lower analog value – always calibrate dry and wet.
Do not keep a resistive probe powered all the time – it corrodes.

quiz.question: On a common resistive module, wetter soil gives…
Why do we calibrate the soil sensor?
quiz.answer: Different sensors and soils give different values
options: Different sensors and soils give different values

quiz.question: Which Arduino pin type reads AO?

notes.principle: A soil-moisture probe estimates water content by measuring a change in electrical resistance or capacitance in the soil.
notes.working: The probe output changes as soil moisture changes. A controller reads the analog/digital signal and uses calibrated thresholds to indicate dry, suitable or wet soil.
advantages: Can be integrated with pumps and alerts
safety: Use a corrosion-resistant capacitive sensor where possible.
Keep exposed electronics and connectors away from water.

title: 16×2 LCD Display
key_points: 16 columns × 2 rows = 32 characters.
An I2C backpack needs only 4 wires: GND, VCC, SDA (A4), SCL (A5).
Common I2C addresses are 0x27 and 0x3F.

quiz.question: How many characters fit on a 16×2 LCD?
I2C pins on Arduino Uno are…
A common I2C LCD address is…

notes.principle: An LCD creates visible characters by controlling liquid-crystal pixels; a 16×2 module displays two rows of 16 characters.
notes.working: The microcontroller sends commands and character data through parallel pins or an I²C backpack. A contrast potentiometer adjusts visibility.
advantages: Low power compared with many displays
safety: Check module voltage and pin order before connecting.
Use a current-limiting backlight arrangement if required by the module.

title: 10 kΩ Potentiometer
summary: Adjust a value by turning a knob.
key_points: Outer pins go to 5 V and GND; the middle (wiper) goes to an analog pin.
analogRead gives 0–1023 as you turn the knob.
map() converts one range to another, e.g. 0–1023 to 0–255.

quiz.question: The potentiometer wiper pin connects to…

notes.principle: A potentiometer is a three-terminal variable resistor; its wiper provides an adjustable fraction of the supply voltage.
notes.working: Connect the two outer terminals to supply and ground and the middle wiper to an analog input. Turning the shaft changes the voltage read by the controller.
disadvantages: Needs analog input and suitable wiring
safety: Use it only within its voltage and power rating.
Avoid forcing the shaft beyond its mechanical travel.

title: Push Buttons
summary: Give a manual input to a circuit.
key_points: A pull-down (or pull-up) resistor keeps the input from floating.
INPUT_PULLUP uses the Arduino’s internal resistor – pressed reads LOW.
Contacts bounce, so wait 20–50 ms (debounce).

quiz.question: Button bounce means…
quiz.answer: Rapid false on/off signals when pressed
options: Rapid false on/off signals when pressed

quiz.question: With INPUT_PULLUP an idle button reads…

notes.principle: A push button is a momentary mechanical switch that opens or closes an electrical path when pressed.
notes.working: The input pin is held at a known logic level using a pull-up or pull-down resistor. Pressing the button changes the pin state; software debounce filters contact bounce.
advantages: Easy to test with digital pins
safety: Use a pull-up or pull-down so the input does not float.
Disconnect power before changing circuit wiring.

title: Buzzer
key_points: An active buzzer beeps when given power; a passive one needs a frequency from tone().
tone(pin, 2000) makes a 2000 Hz sound; noTone(pin) stops it.
Buzzer + goes to the signal pin, − goes to GND.

quiz.question: tone(8, 2000) does what?
quiz.answer: Plays a 2000 Hz sound on pin 8
options: Plays a 2000 Hz sound on pin 8

quiz.question: The buzzer positive (+) pin connects to…

notes.principle: A buzzer converts electrical energy into sound, often using a piezoelectric element or an oscillator circuit.
notes.working: An active buzzer sounds when powered; a passive piezo buzzer needs a changing signal such as tone/PWM to create a pitch.
advantages: Can indicate different states with patterns
disadvantages: Can be irritating if too loud
Some buzzers draw more current than a pin can provide
safety: Use a transistor driver if current exceeds the pin rating.
Keep sound levels comfortable.

title: Red, Yellow & Green LEDs
key_points: An LED has polarity: long leg is the anode (+).
Always add a 220 Ω resistor to limit current.
Traffic order: Red → Green → Yellow → Red.

quiz.question: The longer LED leg is the…
An LED without a resistor may…
To turn an LED on you write…
Which colour means STOP in a traffic light?

notes.principle: An LED emits light when forward current flows through its semiconductor junction.
notes.working: The LED is connected with a series resistor. Current direction determines whether it lights; different colours can indicate system states.
disadvantages: Brightness varies with current and viewing angle
safety: Always use a suitable series resistor.
Check polarity and maximum current before powering.

title: 220 Ω Resistors
key_points: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).
Ohm’s law: V = I × R.
A 220 Ω resistor keeps LED current at a safe level.

quiz.question: Why put a resistor with an LED?

notes.principle: A resistor opposes electric current. A series resistor limits current through an LED and protects it.
notes.working: Ohm’s law relates voltage, current and resistance: V = I × R. Choose resistance from the supply voltage, LED forward voltage and desired current.
advantages: Useful for controlling current and voltage
disadvantages: Fixed resistor values are not adjustable
safety: Choose adequate power rating.
Do not touch a resistor that has become hot.

title: SG90 Servo Motor
summary: Move an arm to a chosen angle.
key_points: Wires: brown = GND, red = 5 V, orange = signal.
The Servo library turns a PWM signal into an angle from 0° to 180°.
Use an external supply when you drive several servos.

notes.principle: A servo motor uses feedback control to move its output shaft to a commanded position.
notes.working: A control pulse train communicates a target angle. The internal controller drives a small motor until the feedback position matches the command.
disadvantages: Limited rotation and torque for small models
safety: Use a suitable external supply for multiple servos and share ground.
Keep fingers clear of moving linkages.

title: Relay Module
summary: Control a separate circuit with a switch.
key_points: A relay is an electrically isolated switch with COM, NO and NC contacts.
Many relay modules switch ON when the input is LOW (active-low).
In school demos use only a low-voltage DC load – never mains.

quiz.question: A safe relay demo load for students is…
Why use a relay?
quiz.answer: A small signal controls another circuit
options: A small signal controls another circuit

quiz.question: Many relay modules turn ON when the input is…

notes.principle: A relay is an electrically operated switch that lets a low-voltage control signal switch a separate circuit.
notes.working: Current in the relay coil creates a magnetic field that moves contacts between normally-open and normally-closed positions. A driver transistor and flyback protection are commonly used.
advantages: Can switch a separate load circuit
Easy to understand as a switch
disadvantages: Slower and larger than semiconductor switches
safety: For student projects use low-voltage DC loads only.
Never wire mains electricity on a student breadboard; use supervised certified equipment.

title: Bluetooth (HC-05 / HC-06)
summary: Send data between Arduino and a phone.
key_points: HC-05/HC-06 talk to Arduino over serial (TX/RX).
Pair the phone first (PIN is commonly 1234 or 0000).
The module RX pin expects 3.3 V – use a voltage divider from Arduino TX.

quiz.question: A common default pairing PIN is…
Arduino TX to HC-05 RX should use…

notes.principle: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless communication technology that exchanges data between paired devices.
notes.working: HC-05/HC-06 modules provide a serial interface. Data sent from the phone is received on the module and passed to the microcontroller UART.
advantages: No internet connection needed for local links
disadvantages: Shorter range than many wide-area technologies
safety: Use a voltage divider or level shifter for a 5 V TX signal into a 3.3 V RX pin.
Pair only with trusted devices.

title: GSM Module
key_points: SIM800/SIM900 modules send SMS and calls using AT commands.
Check that your SIM works with a 2G network.
GSM modules draw high current peaks – use a good power supply.

quiz.question: A GSM module needs…
quiz.answer: A valid SIM and network signal
options: A valid SIM and network signal

quiz.question: A power concern for GSM modules is…

notes.principle: A GSM module connects to a cellular network and exchanges messages or data through a SIM and mobile subscription.
notes.working: The controller sends AT commands over serial. The modem registers on a supported network and can send SMS or make calls depending on the module and service.
applications: Basic telemetry where cellular coverage exists
advantages: Can communicate over large geographic areas
SMS alerts work without local Wi-Fi
disadvantages: Needs network coverage and a SIM plan
Network generations and bands may be unsupported
Power supply must handle current peaks
safety: Check local network compatibility and module power requirements.
Do not share SIM details or personal phone numbers in public project pages.

title: SIM Card
summary: Identify a subscriber on a cellular network.

tamil.query: GSM module SIM card Arduino Tamil

english.query: GSM module SIM card basics IoT

key_points: SIM = Subscriber Identity Module.
It identifies the subscriber on the cellular network.
Check size (micro/nano), network support and PIN lock before use.

quiz.question: Why does a SIM have a PIN?
Before using a SIM in a GSM module, check…
quiz.answer: Size, network support and PIN lock
options: Size, network support and PIN lock

notes.principle: A SIM securely identifies a subscriber to a mobile network and stores authentication information.
notes.working: The modem reads the SIM and uses network authentication to register with the mobile operator. A valid plan and supported network are required.
disadvantages: SIM size and network support must match
PIN locks can prevent automatic startup
safety: Keep SIM PIN/PUK and account information private.
Use a suitable SIM adapter; do not force it into the holder.

title: LoRa / LoRaWAN Module
summary: Send small data over long distances.
key_points: LoRa gives long range with low power but small data rates.
LoRaWAN is the network protocol built on LoRa.
Frequency depends on region (India uses 865–867 MHz) – always attach the antenna first.

quiz.question: Before powering a LoRa module you should…

notes.principle: LoRa is a long-range, low-power radio modulation technique; LoRaWAN defines a network protocol for connecting LoRa devices.
notes.working: End devices transmit small packets to gateways. Gateways forward packets to a network server, which manages devices and application data.
advantages: Long range with low energy use
disadvantages: Low data rate, not for video
Coverage depends on terrain and antenna placement
safety: Use the correct regional frequency plan and legal transmit power.
Attach the correct antenna before transmitting.

title: XBee Module
key_points: XBee modules make low-power wireless (ZigBee / 802.15.4) networks.
Configure them with Digi’s XCTU software.
Modules in one network share the same PAN ID; logic is 3.3 V.

quiz.question: XBee modules in a network share a…

notes.principle: XBee modules provide low-power wireless communication, commonly using IEEE 802.15.4 or Zigbee-compatible networking.
notes.working: Modules are configured with network identifiers and addressing. One module sends packets that another configured module receives.
disadvantages: Different XBee families may not interoperate
safety: Check module voltage and antenna requirements.
Keep network keys and configuration details private.

title: Wi-Fi Module (ESP8266)
summary: Connect a device to Wi-Fi and IoT services.
key_points: ESP8266 joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi networks.
It needs the network name (SSID) and password.
Its pins are 3.3 V – do not feed 5 V directly.

quiz.question: To join a network it needs…

notes.principle: ESP8266 is a microcontroller/Wi-Fi system-on-chip that connects embedded devices to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi networks.
notes.working: The device joins a Wi-Fi access point using its SSID and password. Firmware can host a web page or send sensor data to an IoT service.
disadvantages: Limited pins and memory compared with larger boards
Depends on Wi-Fi coverage and credentials
safety: Never apply 5 V directly to 3.3 V GPIO pins.
Do not hard-code or publish real Wi-Fi passwords.

title: Wireless Receiver / Gateway
key_points: A gateway collects data from nodes and forwards it to the internet or cloud.
It can translate between protocols, e.g. LoRa → Wi-Fi/Ethernet.
Place its antenna high and in the open.

quiz.question: A LoRa gateway forwards data to…

notes.principle: An IoT gateway connects local devices or sensor networks to another network, often forwarding data to a server or cloud.
notes.working: The gateway receives local radio or wired messages, may translate protocols, and forwards validated data over Ethernet, Wi-Fi or cellular links.
applications: Connecting LoRa sensors to cloud dashboards
advantages: Can filter or process data locally
disadvantages: Can become a single point of failure
May introduce latency and security risks
safety: Change default passwords and keep firmware updated.
Place gateways in ventilated, protected locations.

title: Breadboard
key_points: Holes in each short 5-hole strip are connected together.
Long power rails along the edges carry 5 V and GND.
No soldering needed; the centre gap is for chips (ICs).

quiz.question: Holes in one short 5-hole strip are…
Is soldering needed on a breadboard?
The centre gap is meant for…

notes.principle: A breadboard contains connected metal clips under its holes, allowing temporary circuits without soldering.
notes.working: Groups of five holes are commonly connected in rows, while long side rails distribute power. The centre gap separates IC pin rows.
disadvantages: Not suitable for high current or high frequency
safety: Disconnect power before moving wires.
Avoid mains voltage and high-current loads.

title: Jumper Wires
summary: Connect points in a prototype circuit.
key_points: Use red for power, black for GND, other colours for signals.
Press wires in firmly – loose wires cause random behaviour.
Always disconnect power before changing wiring.

quiz.question: Common wire colour for GND is…
Common wire colour for 5 V is…

notes.principle: Jumper wires are insulated conductors that electrically connect points between boards and components.
notes.working: Male/female connector ends fit into breadboards, headers or module sockets. Each wire creates a conductive path between its endpoints.
disadvantages: Messy wiring makes faults harder to find
safety: Use correct wire insulation and connector type.
Disconnect power before rewiring.

title: USB Cable
summary: Power and program a compatible board.

english.query: Arduino connect USB upload first sketch

key_points: Arduino Uno uses a USB Type-B cable for power and uploading.
Some cables are charge-only and cannot upload code.
In the IDE choose the correct Board and Port first.

quiz.question: A USB cable gives the Arduino…

notes.principle: A USB cable carries power and digital data between a computer and a compatible development board.
notes.working: The computer enumerates the board through USB. A data-capable cable allows firmware upload and serial communication; charge-only cables do not.
disadvantages: USB power may be insufficient for motors or radios
safety: Use a known-good data cable.
Do not power high-current loads from a computer USB port.

title: Regulated Power Supply
key_points: A regulated supply keeps output voltage steady.
Uno’s external input is recommended at 7–12 V.
Check polarity; share a common GND if modules use another supply.

quiz.question: Recommended external input for Uno is…
Two separate supplies in one circuit need…

notes.principle: A regulated power supply maintains a stable output voltage despite changes in input voltage or load current within its rating.
notes.working: A regulator uses feedback to adjust its output. Linear and switching supplies regulate in different ways and have different efficiency and heat characteristics.
applications: Supplying external motors or modules with correct ratings
disadvantages: Limited by rated current and thermal capacity
Poor quality supplies can introduce noise
Wrong polarity or voltage can damage parts
safety: Verify voltage, polarity and current rating before connecting.
Use a current-limited supply during first tests.

An Arduino pin gives only about 20 mA – use a relay or transistor for bigger loads.
Never use mains (230 V) on a student breadboard.

quiz.answer: No – use a relay or driver
options: No – use a relay or driver

quiz.question: Safe current from an Uno I/O pin is about…

notes.principle: A demo load is an output device used to show that a controller can switch or regulate a real electrical load.
notes.working: The microcontroller drives a suitable transistor, MOSFET or relay driver. The driver switches the load current while the controller supplies only a control signal.
disadvantages: Loads can draw more current than expected
safety: Use a small, low-voltage DC load only in student demos.
Never connect a mains appliance to a breadboard.

title: Antenna
summary: Help a radio module transmit and receive.
key_points: An antenna sends and receives radio waves.
It must match the module’s frequency (433 MHz, 865 MHz, 2.4 GHz).
Never transmit without the antenna attached.

quiz.question: Choose an antenna that matches the…

notes.principle: An antenna converts electrical radio-frequency energy into electromagnetic waves for transmission and reception.
notes.working: The antenna geometry is designed for a frequency band. It radiates transmitted RF energy and captures incoming radio signals.
advantages: Different designs suit different ranges and devices
Can improve link quality when matched correctly
disadvantages: Performance depends on frequency and placement
Nearby metal and obstacles affect signals
safety: Use an antenna matched to the radio module and band.
Follow radio power and frequency regulations.

title: Voltage Divider / Level Shifter

english.query: voltage divider logic level shifter tutorial

key_points: Voltage divider: Vout = Vin × R2 ÷ (R1 + R2).
A 1 kΩ (top) and 2 kΩ (bottom) divider turns 5 V into about 3.3 V.
A level shifter does this safely in both directions.

quiz.question: Which pair gives about 3.3 V from 5 V (R1 top, R2 bottom)?
Why shift levels?
quiz.answer: To protect 3.3 V pins from 5 V
options: To protect 3.3 V pins from 5 V

notes.principle: A voltage divider uses two resistors to produce a lower voltage; a logic-level shifter safely translates digital signals between voltage domains.
notes.working: For a divider, Vout = Vin × R2 ÷ (R1 + R2). A bidirectional level-shifter module uses switching circuitry for signals travelling in both directions.
applications: Adapting 5 V signals for 3.3 V inputs
advantages: Protects sensitive inputs when designed correctly
Level-shifter modules support multiple signal directions
disadvantages: A resistor divider is not suitable for every fast or bidirectional signal
Output depends on resistor tolerance and load
Incorrect values can still damage inputs
safety: Calculate the output voltage before connecting.
Never assume a 3.3 V input is 5 V tolerant.

title: Smartphone Bluetooth App
summary: Control or monitor a project from a phone.

english.query: control Arduino with phone Bluetooth app

The app sends characters (like ‘A’ or ‘1’) over Bluetooth serial.
The Arduino reads the character and switches an LED, relay or servo.

quiz.question: First step with the app is to…
quiz.answer: Pair the phone with the module
options: Pair the phone with the module

quiz.question: The Arduino reads an incoming character with…

notes.principle: A smartphone Bluetooth app provides a user interface that sends wireless commands to a paired Bluetooth module.
notes.working: The app sends characters or data packets over a Bluetooth serial connection. The controller reads the received data and maps commands to safe output actions.
advantages: No separate physical control panel needed
disadvantages: Range is limited and security must be considered
safety: Pair only with your own project module.
Use command validation and never control hazardous loads from an unsecured app.
